author: copilot
body:
Three bugs in CGI pipe event handling caused CGI responses to abort on normal process exit and left misleading error messages tied to socket syscalls never used on pipes.

## Changes

- **`hasFatalEvents()`** — removed `POLLHUP`; it signals normal pipe EOF (CGI closed stdout), not an error. Only `POLLERR | POLLNVAL` are unrecoverable.

- **`handleCgiFdEvents()`** — `POLLIN & POLLHUP == 0` (different bits), so the original guard was permanently dead when CGI exited cleanly and only `POLLHUP` fired. Replaced with a state-aware check:

```cpp
// POLLHUP means CGI closed stdout (normal EOF). Drain remaining data before read() returns 0.
if (_state == READING_CGI_OUTPUT && (p.revents & (POLLIN | POLLHUP)))
    return _readingFromCgi(_pollfds_vect);
if (p.revents & POLLHUP)
    return false;  // fatal in any other state
```

- **Error messages** — `"send() failed"` → `"write() failed"` and `"recv() failed"` → `"read() failed"` to match the actual POSIX syscalls in use.

author: greenheadhq
body:
## Background

[PR #213](https://github.com/greenheadHQ/nixos-config/pull/213)에서 도입된 nrs worktree lock 시스템이 동작은 하지만, **실사용에서 마찰이 큼**:

| 불편 사항 | 영향 | 빈도 |
|----------|------|------|
| main에서 `nrs` 실행 시 worktree lock에 차단됨 | 일상적인 설정 적용이 불가 (worktree 작업과 무관한데도) | **매일** |
| CC 세션 종료 후 lock 잔류 (stale lock) | 다음 `nrs` 실행 전에 수동 `nrs-unlock` 필수 | 매 CC 세션 |
| worktree 삭제 후에도 lock 잔류 | 삭제된 경로를 참조하는 유령 lock이 다른 작업을 차단 | CC worktree 정리 시 |
| lock 상태 파악 어려움 | `nrs-status`가 stale 여부를 보여주지 않아 판단 불가 | 디버깅 시 |
| PreToolUse guard 오탐 | heredoc, 파일 경로, stdout에 "nrs" 포함 시 무관한 명령 차단 | **매우 빈번** |

**목표**: lock을 "worktree 전용 + 자동 정리" 메커니즘으로 전환하여, 일상 사용(main에서 nrs)에서의 마찰을 제거하면서 LLM 에이전트 간 조율 기능은 유지.

Closes #216

---

## Change Intent Record (CIR)

### 핵심 설계 결정

| 항목 | 기존 (PR #213) | 변경 | 근거 |
|------|---------------|------|------|
| Main worktree lock | 취득함 (다른 worktree와 동일) | **미취득** (경고만 표시) | main은 "최종 적용" 용도. worktree lock이 main을 차단하면 일상 사용 불가 |
| 타임아웃 | 2시간 | **30분** | 2시간은 너무 김. CC 세션은 보통 30분 이내. PID alive 시 연장되므로 장시간 빌드도 보호됨 |
| Stale 감지 | 타임아웃만 | **worktree 삭제 OR 타임아웃** (+ PID alive 가드) | [Issue #216](https://github.com/greenheadHQ/nixos-config/issues/216)의 핵심 요구사항 |
| 자동 정리 | 없음 (수동 `nrs-unlock`만) | **Stop/SessionEnd hook** | CC 세션 종료 시 자동 해제 → stale lock 잔류 방지 |
| PreToolUse guard | Bash 명령 grep으로 lock 충돌 하드 블록 | **완전 제거** | `acquire_nrs_lock()`이 이미 모든 시나리오 처리 + guard의 구조적 오탐 문제 (아래 CIR 참조) |

### 타임아웃 상수 2중 복제 (ADR)

`NRS_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MINUTES=30`이 2개 파일에 중복 존재:
- `rebuild-common.sh` (라이브러리)
- `nrs-lock.sh` (standalone CLI)

**왜 이렇게 했는지**: standalone 스크립트가 `rebuild-common.sh`를 source할 수 없음 (의존성 없이 독립 실행 필수). 각 파일에 동기화 주석(`주의: 이 값은 ... 2곳에서 동일하게 유지해야 함`)을 추가하여 drift 방지.

**기각한 대안**:
- 환경변수로 전달: hook은 Claude Code가 실행하므로 환경변수 제어 불가
- 별도 config 파일: 1개 상수를 위한 파일은 과설계 (YAGNI)

### Main worktree lock 미취득 (ADR)

**왜 이렇게 했는지**: lock의 목적은 "worktree 간 동시 rebuild 방지"이지 "모든 rebuild 직렬화"가 아님. Main은 항상 최종 결과물을 적용하는 용도이므로, worktree의 중간 실험이 main 적용을 차단해서는 안 됨.

**DA 반론과 기각 근거**:
- DA: "main-to-main 동시 실행이 보호되지 않음"
- 기각: main에서 동시에 nrs를 실행하는 시나리오는 극히 드물고, `darwin-rebuild switch` 자체가 sudo 기반으로 OS 레벨에서 직렬화됨

### Stop hook에서 PID-dead lock 정리 (ADR)

**왜 이렇게 했는지**: nrs가 성공적으로 완료된 후 lock이 의도적으로 유지되지만(테스트 보호), PID가 죽은 상태에서 lock은 더 이상 "활성 빌드 보호" 기능을 수행하지 않음. CC 세션 종료 시 자동 정리하여 stale lock 마찰을 제거.

**DA 반론과 기각 근거**:
- DA: "터미널에서 만든 lock을 CC가 삭제할 수 있음"
- 기각: PID가 죽은 lock은 목적(동시 빌드 방지) 완료. 다음 nrs 실행 시 stale 감지로도 정리됨. 자동 정리가 사용자 경험을 크게 개선.

### PreToolUse Guard 제거 (CIR)

> 전체 의사결정 타임라인은 [후속 CIR 코멘트](https://github.com/greenheadHQ/nixos-config/pull/231#issuecomment-4062343904) 참조.

**v1 (PR #213)**: PreToolUse guard 도입 — "LLM이 프롬프트를 무시하고 nrs를 실행할 수 있으므로 하드 블록 필요"

**v2 (이번 PR, e19244b~b144d2a)**: guard에 stale 통과 + main bypass 추가 — lock 시스템 강화에 맞춰 guard도 보강

**v3 (이번 PR, 1228f1a)**: guard 완전 제거

**전환 계기** — 이번 PR 작업 중 발생한 실증적 오탐 6건:

| # | 차단된 명령 | 원인 |
|---|-----------|------|
| 1 | `gh pr edit --body "...nrs-unlock..."` | PR body 텍스트에 "nrs" 포함 |
| 2 | `wc -l .../nrs-lock.sh` | 파일 경로에 "nrs" 포함 |
| 3 | `rm -f /tmp/nrs-state-test` | 테스트 파일명에 "nrs-state" 패턴 |
| 4 | `gh pr comment --body "...nrs..."` | 코멘트 본문에 "nrs" 포함 |
| 5 | `git rm .../nrs-lock-guard.sh` | 파일 경로에 "nrs" 포함 |
| 6 | `git commit -m "...nrs-lock..."` | 커밋 메시지에 "nrs" 포함 |

**근본 원인**: guard의 설계가 "Bash 명령 문자열 전체를 `grep -qE`"하는 방식이므로, 명령어뿐 아니라 **인자, heredoc, 파일 경로, stdout 리다이렉션 텍스트** 모두가 매칭 대상. regex를 아무리 정교하게 만들어도 해결할 수 없는 구조적 한계.

**제거 근거** — guard가 해결하는 문제는 다른 메커니즘이 이미 처리:

| Guard 규칙 | 대체 메커니즘 |
|-----------|-------------|
| 다른 worktree lock → nrs 차단 | `acquire_nrs_lock()` abort + 에러 메시지 |
| Main worktree → 경고 후 진행 | `acquire_nrs_lock()` main 분기 |
| Stale lock → 통과 | `is_stale_lock()` 자동 감지 + 제거 |
| Lock 파일 삭제 방지 | Stop/SessionEnd hook 자동 정리 |
| `nrs-unlock` 차단 | 자동 정리로 수동 해제 필요성 감소 |

**기각한 대안**:
- Guard regex 정교화 → heredoc, 변수 치환, pipe 등 셸 문법 복잡성으로 근본적 해결 불가
- Guard를 명령 파싱(AST) 방식으로 전환 → PreToolUse hook에서 셸 파서 실행은 과설계
- Guard를 PostToolUse로 이동 → nrs 실행은 시스템 상태 변경이므로 사후 차단 무의미

**v1 → v3 교훈**: v1에서 "LLM이 프롬프트를 무시할 수 있다"는 우려로 하드 블록을 선택했으나, 실제로는 **lock 시스템 자체(`acquire_nrs_lock`)가 하드 블록 역할을 수행**하고 있었음. Guard는 중복 레이어였으며, 그 구현 방식(command 문자열 grep)이 구조적으로 오탐에 취약했음.

**최종 trade-off**: guard 제거 시 LLM이 `nrs-unlock`을 직접 실행하거나 lock 파일을 삭제할 수 있게 되지만, (1) Stop/SessionEnd hook이 자동 정리하므로 수동 해제 필요성 자체가 감소, (2) LLM이 lock을 우회해도 `acquire_nrs_lock()`이 충돌을 방지, (3) 오탐으로 인한 사용성 손실이 이론적 안전성 이점보다 압도적으로 큼.

---

## PoC 검증 결과 (2026-03-15)

Stop/SessionEnd hook 안전성을 사전 검증:

| 테스트 | Stop hook 트리거? | 결론 |
|--------|:---:|------|
| Sub-agent (Agent tool) | **No** — SubagentStop만 트리거 | Sub-agent 완료 시 lock 보존 |
| Agent Teams 멤버 (in-process) | **No** — sub-agent와 동일 | Teams 멤버 완료 시 lock 보존 |
| Main agent turn 종료 | **Yes** — 정상 트리거 | Main turn 종료 시 lock 해제 |

→ Stop hook에서 lock 해제는 안전. session_id 매칭 등 복잡한 메커니즘 불필요.

---

## 구현 상세

### 변경 파일 (8개)

| # | 파일 | 변경 유형 | 설명 |
|---|------|----------|------|
| 1 | `modules/shared/scripts/rebuild-common.sh` | 핵심 리팩터링 | `is_stale_lock()` 헬퍼, `acquire_nrs_lock()` main 조기반환 + stale 감지 통합, 타임아웃 30분 |
| 2 | `modules/darwin/scripts/nrs.sh` | 가드 추가 | NO_CHANGES 경로에서 `NRS_LOCK_ACQUIRED` 체크 (main이 다른 worktree lock 삭제 방지) |
| 3 | `modules/shared/scripts/nrs-lock.sh` | 출력 개선 | 타임아웃 30분, worktree 존재 여부/PID 생존/STALE 상태 진단 표시 |
| 4 | `modules/shared/programs/claude/files/hooks/nrs-lock-guard.sh` | **삭제** | PreToolUse guard 완전 제거 (오탐 + 중복 레이어) |
| 5 | `modules/shared/programs/claude/files/hooks/nrs-session-cleanup.sh` | **신규** | Stop/SessionEnd hook — worktree 매칭 + PID 체크 + TOCTOU 방지 |
| 6 | `modules/shared/programs/claude/files/settings.json` | hook 변경 | PreToolUse Bash matcher 제거 + Stop/SessionEnd hook 등록 |
| 7 | `modules/shared/programs/claude/default.nix` | symlink 변경 | guard symlink 제거 + cleanup hook symlink 추가 |
| 8 | `modules/shared/programs/cheat/cheatsheets/nrs/command` | docs | lock 동작 설명 업데이트 (30분, main 미취득, 자동 정리) |

### Lock 생명주기 (변경 후)

```
nrs 실행 (main worktree):
  acquire_nrs_lock()
  ├─ lock 없음 → return 0 (lock 미취득)
  ├─ lock 있음 + stale → 경고 + 자동 제거 + return 0
  └─ lock 있음 + active → "Worktree lock active" 경고 + return 0
  → 빌드/switch 정상 진행 (NRS_LOCK_ACQUIRED=false)

nrs 실행 (worktree):
  acquire_nrs_lock()
  ├─ lock 없음 → tmpfile + ln으로 원자적 생성
  ├─ lock 있음 + stale → 제거 + 새 lock 생성
  ├─ lock 있음 + 같은 worktree → re-entry (PID 체크)
  └─ lock 있음 + 다른 worktree + active → abort
  → 빌드/switch 진행

CC 세션 종료:
  Stop hook (LLM turn 종료) 또는 SessionEnd hook (세션 종료)
  ├─ lock 없음 → exit 0
  ├─ worktree 불일치 → exit 0 (다른 worktree lock 보존)
  ├─ PID alive → exit 0 (활성 빌드 보호)
  ├─ PID 재확인 불일치 → exit 0 (TOCTOU 방지)
  └─ worktree 일치 + PID dead → rm -f (자동 정리)
```

> **Note**: PreToolUse guard는 제거됨. lock 충돌 방지는 `acquire_nrs_lock()` 자체가 담당.

---

## DA (Devil's Advocate) 피드백 루프

3라운드 DA 리뷰 수행 (`codex exec review --base main`).

### Round 1
| 지적 | 심각도 | 판정 | 조치 |
|------|--------|------|------|
| main lock 미취득 → 동시 rebuild 가능 | P1 | **기각** (설계 의도) | — |
| `is_stale_lock()` PID 미체크 → 장시간 빌드 stale 오판 | P2 | **수용** | PID alive 시 stale 아님 가드 추가 (4곳) |
| `nrs-session-cleanup.sh` owner-blind rm | P2 | **수용** | PID alive 체크 추가 |

### Round 2
| 지적 | 심각도 | 판정 | 조치 |
|------|--------|------|------|
| `nrs-lock-guard.sh`에 main worktree 바이패스 없음 | P2 | **수용** → 이후 guard 자체 제거로 무효화 | ~~git-dir == git-common-dir 체크~~ |
| `nrs-session-cleanup.sh` TOCTOU race | P3 | **수용** | rm 직전 PID 재확인 (변경 감지 시 abort) |

### Round 3
| 지적 | 심각도 | 판정 | 조치 |
|------|--------|------|------|
| main lock 미취득 재반론 | P1 | **기각** (R1과 동일) | — |
| Stop hook이 터미널 lock 삭제 가능 | P2 | **기각** (PID dead lock은 목적 완료) | — |

### CodeRabbit 리뷰
| 지적 | 심각도 | 판정 | 조치 |
|------|--------|------|------|
| Guard main bypass를 same-worktree 체크보다 먼저 배치 | Minor | **수용** → 이후 guard 자체 제거로 무효화 | ~~main bypass 순서 변경~~ |
| Session token + mkdir guard로 cleanup 직렬화 | Critical | **기각** | 기술적 실현 불가 (`nrs`가 session_id에 접근 불가) + YAGNI |

author: janmaarten-a11y
body:
## Initial scaffolding for HomepageMD v0.1

Sets up the complete project structure, core modules, configuration, Docker deployment, and test suite.

### What's included

**Server (`src/server/`)**
- `index.js` — HTTP server with path-based MPA routing, SSE for live updates, `fs.watch` file watcher
- `config.js` — Environment variable configuration (`PORT`, `DEFAULT_PAGE`, `AUTH_TOKEN`, etc.)
- `parser.js` — Custom Markdown parser: `# title`, `## category`, `### subcategory`, `- [title](url)`, `- description:`, `- icon:`
- `favicon.js` — Favicon resolution chain (manual → inline → cache → direct fetch → DuckDuckGo → placeholder) with SSRF protection (private IP blocking)
- `renderer.js` — Server-rendered HTML with semantic markup (`aria-labelledby`, `role="list"`, proper heading hierarchy)
- `writer.js` — Interface stubs for v0.3 write-back functionality

**Client (`src/public/`)**
- `styles/main.css` — CSS cascade layers (`config`, `resets`, `components`, `utilities`), OKLCH color tokens, dark mode via `prefers-color-scheme`, logical properties, responsive grid
- `scripts/app.js` — SSE listener for live page updates

**Configuration & deployment**
- `package.json` — ES modules, Node.js 22+, `node:test` runner
- `Dockerfile` — `node:22-alpine` with `HEALTHCHECK`
- `docker-compose.yml` — Volumes for `bookmarks/`, `icons/`, `custom.css`, named volume for `favicon-cache/`
- `.editorconfig` — 2-space indent, UTF-8, LF
- `.gitignore` — `node_modules/`, `favicon-cache/`
- `custom.css` — Documented user override file at project root (easy Docker volume mount)

**Content**
- `bookmarks/homepage.md` — Default starter bookmarks file
- `icons/default.svg` — Generic placeholder favicon

**Tests (34 passing)**
- `test/server/parser.test.js` — 15 tests: title extraction, categories, subcategories, bookmarks, metadata, empty files, malformed input
- `test/server/favicon.test.js` — 19 tests: SSRF private IP blocking (IPv4, IPv6, mapped), domain extraction
- `test/fixtures/` — valid.md, malformed.md, empty.md

### Architecture decisions made in this PR

| Decision | Detail |
|---|---|
| Dark mode | Same tokens redefined in `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` — no `-dark` suffix |
| Routing | Path-based MPA: `/homepage`, `/kids`, etc. Server renders full HTML per route |
| Default page | Configurable via `DEFAULT_PAGE` env var (defaults to `homepage`) |
| Auth | Optional `AUTH_TOKEN` env var for write endpoints |
| Metadata syntax | `- description: text` and `- icon: url` (extensible key-value pattern) |
| Error handling | Silently skip unrecognized/malformed Markdown syntax |
| Favicon cache | Named Docker volume, refresh on write, configurable TTL |
| SSRF | Block private IPs (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x, 127.x, 169.254.x, ::1, fc/fd, fe80) |
| `custom.css` | Project root (not inside `src/`) for clean Docker volume mounting |

### How to test

```bash
npm test          # 34 tests pass
npm run dev       # starts server at http://localhost:3000
```

author: ruanps01
body:
## Summary
Fixed a bug where the countdown effect was accessing stale quiz data from a ref instead of the current state, causing questions to fail to load properly when the quiz data arrives after the countdown has already started (e.g., after a page reload).

## Changes
- Changed `quizRef.current?.questions[qIdx]` to `quiz?.questions[qIdx]` in the countdown effect to use the quiz state instead of the ref
- Added `quiz` to the dependency array of the countdown effect so it re-runs when quiz data becomes available
- Updated the comment to explain the rationale: using state ensures the effect re-runs when quiz becomes available after SYNC_STATE arrives, even if NEXT_COUNTDOWN has already started the countdown with quiz still null

## Implementation Details
This fixes a race condition where:
1. NEXT_COUNTDOWN message arrives and starts the countdown with `quiz` still null
2. SYNC_STATE message arrives later with the actual quiz data
3. The countdown effect was using `quizRef.current` (which may not be updated) instead of the `quiz` state
4. By adding `quiz` to dependencies, the effect now re-runs when quiz data is available, allowing the question to load correctly

## Summary

This PR adds native Kubernetes service account token authentication to Flipt as a first-class authentication method alongside the existing token-based and OIDC methods. Kubernetes pods can now authenticate against Flipt's API by presenting their service account tokens, which are validated via the cluster's OIDC discovery endpoint.

## Key Changes

### Protobuf & API Layer (5 files)
- Extended `Method` enum with `METHOD_KUBERNETES = 3` in `auth.proto`
- Added `VerifyServiceAccountRequest/Response` messages and `AuthenticationMethodKubernetesService` gRPC service
- Regenerated Go bindings (`auth.pb.go`, `auth_grpc.pb.go`, `auth.pb.gw.go`)
- Added HTTP rule mapping for `POST /auth/v1/method/kubernetes/verify` in `flipt.yaml`

### Configuration Layer (5 files)
- Added `AuthenticationMethodKubernetesConfig` struct with `IssuerURL`, `CAPath`, `ServiceAccountTokenPath` fields
- Integrated into `AuthenticationMethods` struct with `AllMethods()` support
- In-cluster defaults for issuer URL, CA path, and token path
- JSON Schema and `default.yml` updated with kubernetes method entry

### Core Server Implementation (1 file, 205 lines)
- `internal/server/auth/method/kubernetes/server.go` — OIDC-based token verification using `coreos/go-oidc/v3`
- Custom CA transport for Kubernetes API server TLS verification
- Claims extraction (subject, namespace, service account name) with metadata persistence

### Server Wiring (1 file)
- `internal/cmd/auth.go` — Conditional registration in both gRPC and HTTP transport layers with skip-auth for verify endpoint

### Tests & Examples (4 files)
- Integration tests with mock OIDC provider, bufconn, and memory store (4 test cases: empty token, invalid token, valid token, expired token)
- Config loading and validation test cases (valid config, invalid CA path)
- Cleanup service test assertion for `METHOD_KUBERNETES`
- Example Kubernetes deployment configuration

## Validation Results
- **Build**: `go build ./...` — 0 errors
- **Lint**: `buf lint` and `go vet` — 0 issues
- **Tests**: 20/20 test packages pass, including all 4 new Kubernetes auth tests
- **Runtime**: Binary starts, `GET /auth/v1/method` exposes METHOD_KUBERNETES with `sessionCompatible: false`

## Metrics
- **Files changed**: 16 (5 new, 11 modified)
- **Lines**: +1,315 / -182 (net +1,133)
- **Commits**: 11

## Remaining Work for Production
- Real Kubernetes cluster integration testing
- Production environment configuration (secrets, CA certs)
- Security audit review
- Performance/load testing

author: simonmau
body:
## Summary

This branch removes the old Sieve-based paging surface and replaces it with a native pagination/filter/sort stack, while expanding CRUD infrastructure around concurrency, soft delete, OpenAPI metadata, provider support, and utility APIs.

## What changed

### 1. Replaced the Sieve API surface with native pagination
- Removed `IApiSieve` / `ApiSieve`
- Added `IApiPagination` / `ApiPagination`
- Added a full internal pagination engine:
  - `IPaginationProcessor` / `PaginationProcessor`
  - query model + deserializer
  - filter operators
  - member-path resolution
  - custom filter methods
  - custom sort methods
- Kept Sieve-style query syntax compatibility for filters and sorts

### 2. Added richer OpenAPI integration for pagination
- Added OpenAPI support for pagination query parameters
- Supports both Swashbuckle and `Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi`
- Added support for:
  - inferred pagination model types
  - explicit `[PaginationOpenApiType]`
  - nested fields
  - custom filter/sort methods
- `openapi.json` now includes:
  - clearer descriptions
  - examples for `filters` and `sorts`
  - machine-readable `x-tools-dotnet-pagination` metadata

### 3. Added optimistic concurrency support
- Added concurrent CRUD interfaces and base implementations:
  - `IConcurrentCrudRepo...`
  - `IConcurrentCrudDtoRepo...`
  - `IConcurrentCrudService...`
- Added configurable concurrency token support via `CrudConcurrencyConfiguration`
- Supported token styles:
  - `UpdatedTimestamp`
  - SQL Server `rowversion`
  - PostgreSQL `xmin`
  - custom token properties / custom token types
- Added `ApiConcurrentModificationError`
- Added concurrency-aware delete/restore flows
- Added repo/service support to fetch or work with concurrency tokens explicitly

### 4. Added explicit soft-delete lifecycle APIs
- Added explicit lifecycle operations for soft-deletable entities:
  - soft delete
  - restore
  - hard delete
- Standardized read behavior around `SoftDeleteQueryMode`
- Removed repo methods like:
  - `GetAllIncludingDeletedAsync(...)`
  - `GetAllDeletedAsync(...)`
  - `GetByIdIncludingDeletedAsync(...)`
- Replaced them with `SoftDeleteQueryMode`-based overloads

### 5. Added provider-neutral database exception translation
- Added shared `CrudDbUpdateExceptionTranslator`
- Removed hard dependency on PostgreSQL-only exception handling
- Added translation coverage for SQL Server and PostgreSQL conflict/dependency errors
- Mapped concurrency exceptions consistently to API errors

### 6. Added cancellation token support
- Threaded `CancellationToken` through repo, DTO repo, service, and paging/query helpers
- Updated async paging execution to pass cancellation tokens through EF Core async calls

### 7. Improved pagination runtime performance
- Added metadata caches inside `PaginationProcessor` for:
  - field-path resolution
  - custom filter method lookup
  - custom sort method lookup
- Reduced paged-query overhead by deserializing pagination once and reusing the parsed model
- Added focused tests and benchmarks around pagination processing

### 8. Reworked enum/string casing utilities
- Added fast `StringCaseExtensions`
- Added `StringCaseType`
- Replaced specialized enum converters with:
  - `EnumCaseConverter`
- Removed:
  - `SnakeCaseEnumConverter<T>`
  - `UpperKebabCaseEnumConverter<TEnum>`
- Added compatibility coverage against the old snake-case behavior
- Added broad real-world identifier test coverage

### 9. Added utility and infrastructure improvements
- Added `GZipCompressionHelper`
- Updated `TimestampsInterceptor`
  - preserves `CreatedTimestamp` on update
  - continues to manage `UpdatedTimestamp`
- Added global usings updates and enum namespace cleanup
- Switched solution/build flow to `tools-dotnet.slnx`
- Updated CI, line endings, editor config, and git attributes

## Testing

Test coverage was expanded significantly across the new feature areas:
- pagination processor and deserializer
- custom sort/filter methods
- pagination OpenAPI output
- Sieve-style compatibility
- soft-delete lifecycle
- concurrency behavior
- provider-specific exception translation
- string casing and enum conversion

Integration coverage now includes container-backed tests for:
- SQL Server
- PostgreSQL

Latest full test run on this branch:
- `488/488` tests passing

## Breaking / migration notes

### Removed or replaced APIs
- `IApiSieve` / `ApiSieve`
  - replaced by `IPaginationProcessor` / `PaginationProcessor` and `IApiPagination` / `ApiPagination`
- Repo deleted-row helper methods
  - replaced by `SoftDeleteQueryMode` overloads
- `SnakeCaseEnumConverter<T>`
  - replaced by `new EnumCaseConverter(StringCaseType.SnakeCase)`
- `UpperKebabCaseEnumConverter<TEnum>`
  - replaced by `new EnumCaseConverter(StringCaseType.UpperKebabCase)`

### Behavioral changes
- Soft-deleted rows are now accessed consistently through `SoftDeleteQueryMode`
- `CreatedTimestamp` is treated as server-owned and is no longer effectively client-writable during updates
- OpenAPI output for pagination is much richer and now includes structured metadata

## Notes

This branch is effectively a foundation update:
- deprecates the old Sieve-specific surface
- keeps Sieve-style query syntax compatibility
- adds a first-class internal pagination system
- makes CRUD infrastructure more production-ready across concurrency, soft delete, provider support, and documentation

body:
Creates an Android app that acts as a local-network WebSocket relay between a browser-based camera source and one or more browser-based monitor viewers — no native camera access required on the Android device itself. ## Architecture ``` Browser (camera device) ──WS /ws/camera──► Android (port 8080) ──WS /ws/monitor──► Browser(s) (monitor) getUserMedia() → JPEG frames relay live feed ``` ## Components - **`WebServer.java`** — `NanoWSD` subclass; serves HTML over HTTP and relays binary JPEG WebSocket frames from one camera sender to N monitor receivers via `CopyOnWriteArraySet` - **`ServerService.java`** — foreground `Service` wrapping the server so it survives backgrounding - **`MainActivity.java`** — shows camera/monitor LAN URLs with copy buttons; polls server state (camera connected, monitor count) every second - **`assets/camera.html`** — `getUserMedia` → canvas → JPEG blob → WebSocket; configurable FPS (5–30) and quality (low/med/high); includes inline instructions for enabling camera over HTTP in Chrome/Firefox - **`assets/monitor.html`** — receives binary frames via WebSocket, renders via `URL.createObjectURL`, shows live FPS counter, auto-reconnects on disconnect ## Build Single Maven Central dependency: `org.nanohttpd:nanohttpd-websocket:2.3.1` ```bash ./gradlew assembleDebug # requires JDK 17, Android SDK API 34 ``` ## Caveat `getUserMedia` requires HTTPS on non-localhost origins in most browsers. The camera page includes on-screen instructions for the required Chrome flag (`#unsafely-treat-insecure-origin-as-secure`) and Firefox `about:config` toggle (`media.devices.insecure.enabled`). > [!WARNING] > >

author: slepp
body:
## Summary

Adds `std::channel::channel` — a bounded MPSC (multi-producer, single-consumer) channel module to the standard library.

## API

```hew
import std::channel::channel;

let (tx, rx) = channel.new(8);

// Sender
tx.send("hello");
let tx2 = tx.clone();   // multi-producer
tx.close();

// Receiver
let msg = rx.recv();       // blocking
let msg = rx.try_recv();   // non-blocking
rx.close();
```

## Implementation

- **Runtime** (`hew-runtime/src/channel.rs`): 10 `#[no_mangle] extern "C"` FFI functions wrapping Rust's `std::sync::mpsc::sync_channel`. Includes 5 unit tests covering create/free, send/recv, closed channel, try_recv, and multi-producer.
- **Stdlib** (`std/channel/channel.hew`): Opaque `Sender`/`Receiver` types with trait-based methods, following the semaphore/stream pattern.
- **E2E test**: `channel_mpsc` demonstrates two producers cloning a sender and a consumer draining via `recv()` loop.

## Design notes

- `recv()` returns a valid empty string (`""`) on channel closure rather than NULL, because Hew's `hew_string_equals` treats NULL ≠ `""`.
- `try_recv()` returns NULL on empty/closed (consistent with stream's non-blocking semantics).

## Testing

- `make test`: 463/463 pass ✅
- `make lint`: clean ✅

author: deseltrus
body:
## Problem

### 1. gsd config doesn't hydrate existing keys
Running `gsd config` from the terminal shows API keys as "not configured" even when they exist in `~/.gsd/agent/auth.json`. The `config` subcommand in `cli.ts` creates an `AuthStorage` and calls `runOnboarding()` but skips `loadStoredEnvKeys()` — so environment variables aren't populated from stored credentials.

### 2. No way to configure API keys from within a running session
Tool API keys (Tavily, Brave, Context7, Jina, Groq) can only be set via `gsd config` in the terminal — which requires exiting the current session. There's no slash command equivalent.

### 3. Native Anthropic search not visible in /search-provider
When using a Claude model, native web search is automatically active but `/search-provider` doesn't mention this.

## Architecture: How Config Flows

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    KEY STORAGE & HYDRATION                       │
│                                                                 │
│  ~/.gsd/agent/auth.json                                         │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐                │
│  │ tavily:   { type: "api_key", key: "tvly-…" }│                │
│  │ brave:    { type: "api_key", key: "BSA…"  } │                │
│  │ context7: { type: "api_key", key: "c7-…"  } │                │
│  │ jina:     { type: "api_key", key: "…"     } │                │
│  │ groq:     { type: "api_key", key: "…"     } │                │
│  └──────────────────┬──────────────────────────┘                │
│                     │                                           │
│          loadStoredEnvKeys()                                    │
│                     │                                           │
│                     ▼                                           │
│  process.env                                                    │
```

author: azmatsiddique
body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?
This PR fixes an issue where the CSV reader inconsistently parses empty quoted strings (`""`) when the `escape` option is set to an empty string (`""`). 

Previously, if `escape=""` was used, mid-line empty quoted strings were correctly resolved to an empty string, but the last column resolved to a literal `"` character. This occurred because Spark Maps `escape=""` to `\u0000`, which univocity’s parser relies on. At the end of a line, without a trailing delimiter, univocity misinterprets the second `"` as an escaped quote rather than a closing quote.

The fix introduces a post-processing step in `UnivocityParser.parseLine` to detect this specific condition (a single quote character as the last token when `escape` is `\u0000`) and replace it with the configured `emptyValueInRead`.

### Why are the changes needed?
To ensure consistent parsing of CSV data regardless of whether an empty quoted string appears in the middle of a line or at the end of a line.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
Yes, it fixes a bug where users were receiving incorrect data (a literal quote instead of an empty/null value) for the last column in a row under specific CSV configurations (e.g. `escape=""`, `quote="\""`, `sep=";"`).

### How was this patch tested?
Added a new regression test in [CSVSuite.scala](cci:7://file:///Users/azmatsiddique/spark/sql/core/src/test/scala/org/apache/spark/sql/execution/datasources/csv/CSVSuite.scala:0:0-0:0):
`"SPARK-46959: CSV reader reads data inconsistently depending on column position"`

The test verifies that an empty quoted string behaves identically in the mid-line position (column c) and the end-of-line position (column d) when configured with `escape=""` and `nullValue=""`. 

Verified that both `CSVv1Suite` and `CSVv2Suite` pass without regressions.

### Was this patch authored or co-authored using generative AI tooling?
No

### Motivation
- Boot UI was too small and the boot animation advanced too quickly on Pi Zero 2W, and the trig-based orb animation is CPU-heavy for the constrained device.
- Runtime `font_scale` was not being applied to the boot screen, so fonts needed explicit sizing to be readable on the physical 240x280 display.

### Description
- Increased boot auto-advance time from `3.0` to `8.0` seconds in `device/screens/boot.py` so diagnostics/animation remain visible longer.
- Replaced floating-point trig orb rendering with an 8-step integer-position loop in `device/screens/boot.py` to reduce per-frame CPU work on Pi Zero 2W.
- Switched boot title/status font loading to explicit sizes (`32` for title, `10` for status) in `device/screens/boot.py` because the boot screen bypasses runtime `font_scale`.
- Updated `server/data/ui_settings.json` to set `font_scale` to `2.0` and added matching `font_size_overrides` for `title/body/small/hint`.
- Adjusted the shell-flow test in `tests/test_phase2_shell_flow.py` to assert the new `8` second auto-advance behavior.

### Testing
- Ran `pytest -q`; after updating the timing test the suite passed with `299 passed, 1 warning`.
- An initial `pytest -q` run failed due to the test still expecting a 3s auto-advance, then the test was updated and the final test run succeeded.

author: taigrr
body:
## Summary

Adds WebSocket log streaming to `grlx serve` so the web UI's log viewer page can display real-time cook events.

### New endpoints

- **`GET /api/v1/logs/stream`** — WebSocket upgrade. Subscribes to NATS `grlx.cook.*.*` subjects and streams parsed `LogEntry` JSON messages. Supports `level` and `source` query param filters.
- **`GET /api/v1/logs`** — REST endpoint returning recent log entries from an in-memory ring buffer (200 entries). Supports `level`, `source`, and `limit` query params.

### Architecture

- `logHub` singleton subscribes to NATS cook events once and fans out to all connected WebSocket clients
- Each client connection filters independently by level severity and source type
- Ring buffer stores recent entries for the REST endpoint (no persistence needed)
- Ping/pong keepalive with automatic client cleanup on disconnect
- `gorilla/websocket` for WebSocket upgrade handling (per coding standards)

### Web UI integration

The `grlx-web-ui` log viewer page (`useLogStream` hook) connects to `ws://localhost:5407/api/v1/logs/stream` — this PR provides the server-side implementation.

### Tests

- `matchesFilter` — level and source filtering logic
- `splitSubject` — NATS subject parsing  
- Ring buffer store/get with filtering and limits
- WebSocket stream with broadcast verification
- WebSocket level filter (debug filtered, error passes)
- WebSocket source filter
- Hub broadcast fan-out with per-client filters
- All tests pass with `-race` flag

### OpenAPI

Updated `openapi.yaml` with both endpoint definitions and `LogEntry` schema.

author: copilot
body:
Custom user attributes configured in federation mappers and user claims were being silently dropped from `access_token` and `userinfo` responses when `claim.name` was stored as an empty string — causing claims to disappear entirely rather than defaulting to the attribute name.

## Root cause

`dict.get(key, default)` only returns `default` when the key is **absent**, not when it is `''`:

```python
# Before — empty string bypasses the fallback, claim silently dropped
claim_name = config.get('claim.name', user_attr)

# After — empty OR missing claim.name both fall back to the attribute name
claim_name = config.get('claim.name') or user_attr
```

This mirrors Keycloak's behavior: if the admin leaves the "Claim Name" field blank, the attribute name is used as-is.

## Changes

- **`mapper_service.py`** — `_apply_user_attribute_mapper`: use `or` instead of `.get(key, default)` so an empty-string `claim.name` falls back to `user_attr` instead of being passed to the `if not claim_name: return token` guard.

- **`tests/federation/test_attribute_sync.py`** — new `TestClaimNameAlwaysRespected` class with four regression tests:
  - `test_claim_name_equals_attribute_name` — `user.attribute='photo'` + `claim.name='photo'` → token key is exactly `'photo'` (no renaming to `'avatar'`, `'picture'`, etc.)
  - `test_claim_name_empty_falls_back_to_attribute_name` — `claim.name=''` → claim still appears under the attribute name
  - `test_any_custom_attribute_uses_configured_claim_name` — any custom attribute (`department`, `employee_id`, …) surfaces under its exact configured name
  - `test_federation_mapper_auto_creates_correct_claim_name` — end-to-end: federation mapper auto-creates a protocol mapper with `claim.name == internal_attribute`; after sync the userinfo response contains the attribute under that exact key

author: br1an67
body:
## Summary
- Problem: `openclaw update` on a git install defaults to the `dev` channel (pulling from `main`) even when checked out to a release tag like `v2026.2.15`. This causes users on stable releases to unexpectedly jump to unreleased code.
- Why it matters: Users on stable git installs get silently moved to unreleased development code when running `openclaw update`.
- What changed: Replaced the hardcoded `DEFAULT_GIT_CHANNEL` fallback with `resolveEffectiveUpdateChannel()`, which detects the current git tag/branch and returns `stable` for release tags, `beta` for beta tags, and `dev` only for branch-based checkouts.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): Explicit `--channel` flags and `update.channel` config take precedence as before. Package installs are unaffected.

## Change Type
- [x] Bug fix

## Scope
- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [x] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR
- Closes #18702

## User-visible / Behavior Changes
Git installs checked out to a release tag now default to the `stable` update channel instead of `dev`.

## Security Impact
- New permissions/capabilities? No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- New/changed network calls? No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- Data access scope changed? No

## Repro + Verification
### Steps
1. Clone openclaw and checkout a release tag: `git checkout v2026.2.15`
2. Run `openclaw update` (no flags)
### Expected
- Updates to the latest stable release tag
### Actual
- Before fix: Pulls from `main`, moves to unreleased commits

## Evidence
- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- pnpm tsgo passes with no new errors

## Human Verification
- Verified scenarios: pnpm tsgo passes; reviewed diff matches issue description
- Edge cases checked: explicit --channel flag still takes precedence; config-stored channel still takes precedence; branch-based git checkouts still default to dev
- What you did NOT verify: runtime end-to-end testing with actual git install update

## Review Conversations
- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.

- Backward compatible? Yes (behavior change only affects the default when no explicit channel is configured)
- Config/env changes? No

## Risks and Mitigations
None

author: ivanov-gv
body:
This PR replaces the custom GraphQL client implementation with the `shurcooL/githubv4` library, which provides a type-safe GraphQL client for GitHub's API.

## Summary
Migrated from a manual JSON-based GraphQL implementation to the `shurcooL/githubv4` library across all service packages. This improves type safety, reduces boilerplate, and leverages a well-maintained community library.

## Key Changes

- **Replaced custom GraphQL client**: Removed the manual `GraphQLClient` implementation in `internal/github/graphql.go` and replaced it with `githubv4.Client`. The new implementation uses a custom `tokenTransport` to inject Bearer token authentication.

- **Updated service packages**: Modified `pr`, `review`, and `comment` services to use `*githubv4.Client` instead of `*gh.GraphQLClient`.

- **Converted query definitions**: Transformed all GraphQL query strings into Go struct definitions using `graphql` struct tags for proper type mapping:
  - Replaced JSON struct tags with `graphql` tags for query field mapping
  - Used `githubv4` scalar types (`String`, `Int`, `Boolean`, `DateTime`, `URI`) for type safety
  - Added inline fragment support for union types (e.g., `prReviewerNode` for User/Team reviewers)

- **Updated query execution**: Changed from string-based queries with manual variable marshaling to structured queries:
  - Added `context.Background()` to all `Query()` calls
  - Converted variables to use `githubv4` scalar types
  - Simplified error handling with direct struct-based queries

- **Added type conversions**: Added explicit type conversions from `githubv4` scalar types to Go primitives throughout mapping functions (e.g., `int(n.Number)`, `string(n.Title)`).

- **Improved DateTime handling**: Converted `githubv4.DateTime` values to formatted strings using `.UTC().Format("2006-01-02T15:04:05Z")`.

## Notable Implementation Details

- The `tokenTransport` implements `http.RoundTripper` to inject OAuth Bearer tokens on every request
- Query structures now use struct tags for both repository/PR selection and field pagination (e.g., `graphql:"assignees(first: 20)"`)
- Inline fragments for union types are handled via separate struct fields with `graphql:"... on Type"` tags
- All GraphQL query strings have been eliminated in favor of declarative struct definitions

body:
## What
Replace the hardcoded 8-week window in `GET /api/reflect/weeks` with a data-driven range covering all sessions in history. Cap `WeekSelector` dot indicators to 8 most recent weeks while keeping arrow navigation across the full range.

Closes #183

## Why
Users with sessions older than 8 weeks could not navigate to them — the weeks were invisible to the UI. The CASE-bucketing SQL approach also couldn't scale beyond the hardcoded window.

## How

**Server (`server/src/routes/reflect.ts`):**
- Query `MIN(started_at)` from sessions to find earliest week
- Generate all weeks from earliest through current (can be 50+ for long-time users)
- Replace CASE-bucketing SQL with `GROUP BY date(started_at, 'weekday 1', '-7 days')` — one scan, one row per week with sessions
- Handle edge case: no sessions → return empty array

**Dashboard (`dashboard/src/components/patterns/WeekSelector.tsx`):**
- Cap dot rendering to 8 most recent weeks (cosmetic indicator only)
- Arrow navigation unchanged — operates on full `navigableWeeks` list
- Current week dot always visible: if it falls outside the 8-dot window (user browsing old history), replace the 8th dot slot with the current week

## Schema Impact
- SQLite schema changed: no
- Types changed: no
- Server API changed: response shape unchanged (`{ weeks: WeekInfo[] }`)
- Backward compatible: yes

## Testing
- `pnpm build` passes from repo root (zero errors)
- Two focused file changes; no new files, no new dependencies

body:
## Summary

When the IEC API returns partial data for an hour (e.g., 23:00 exists but 23:15/23:30/23:45 are missing), the statistics fetch gets stuck because `_insert_statistics` skips hours with fewer than 4 readings. The next refresh then re-attempts the same hour indefinitely.

This PR adds an `update_statistics_date` service that inserts a zero-value statistic record at a target hour, naturally advancing the DB's "last statistics" point so the next refresh continues from there.

## Changes

- **coordinator.py**: Added `asyncio.Lock` (`_statistics_lock`) to protect concurrent statistics operations, wrapped `_insert_statistics` with the lock, added `set_statistics_from_date` method with full validation, normalized `device_number` by stripping leading zeros
- **__init__.py**: Registered `update_statistics_date` service
- **services.yaml**: Added service definition
- **translations/en.json**: Added English translations
- **translations/he.json**: Added Hebrew translations

## Validation

The service validates:
1. Device number format (strips leading zeros)
2. Datetime format (ISO)
3. Not in the future
4. Not older than 30 days
5. Hour-aligned (minute/second must be 0)
6. Device belongs to a known contract
7. Target date is after last statistics
8. No valid statistics already exist at target hour

## Test Plan

1. Call service: `hass.services.async_call("iec", "update_statistics_date", {"datetime": "2024-01-16T01:00:00", "device_number": "12345"})`
2. Verify validation rejects dates before last statistics
3. Verify validation rejects hours that already have valid statistics
4. Verify the next `_insert_statistics` cycle picks up from the new hour

body:
`!naama` previously placed overlays from coarse person bounds, which caused poor alignment/scaling on real photos. This change upgrades placement to use facial/hand/head/body anchors and shoulder orientation so accessories track subject geometry more accurately.

- **Pose + segmentation multi-pass inference**
  - Keep person extraction via segmentation.
  - Add a fast pose pass (`task="pose"`) and derive pose model name from the configured segmentation model (`*-seg` → `*-pose`).

- **Landmark-driven accessory anchoring**
  - Compute anchors for:
    - top of head
    - mouth (nose-derived)
    - left/right hands (wrist-derived)
    - body center (shoulder-derived)
  - Use these anchors to place hat, suit, gloves, and cigar instead of bbox-only offsets.

- **Orientation-aware overlay transforms**
  - Estimate shoulder tilt from left/right shoulder keypoints.
  - Apply accessory-specific rotation scaling to better match subject posture.
  - Preserve deterministic composition behavior and existing asset loading flow.

- **Robust fallback behavior**
  - If pose keypoints are missing/low-confidence, fallback to mask-based anchor heuristics (no hard failure).
  - Keep current failure behavior for missing required assets unchanged.

- **Code clarity in tuned geometry constants**
  - Replace inline magic ratios with named constants for key offsets/rotation scales (mouth offset, hand fallback ratios, body center fallback, per-accessory rotation multipliers).

```python
pose_keypoints = _extract_pose_keypoints(
    image_rgb,
    model_name=model_name,
    confidence_threshold=confidence_threshold,
    model_loader=model_loader,
)
anchors = _build_naama_anchors(person_mask, pose_keypoints)

_paste_scaled_overlay(
    composed,
    hat_image.convert("RGBA"),
    center_x=anchors.top_head[0],
    center_y=anchors.top_head[1] - int(person_height * 0.16),
    width=int(person_width * 0.95),
    angle_degrees=anchors.shoulder_angle_degrees * _HAT_ROTATION_SCALE,
)
```

body: Adds LLM-generated recipes for meals, stored and shared across users based on a new database model that tracks shared meal proposals and individual portion factors. The core requirement was to ensure that meals originating from the same LLM generation are explicitly linked in the database, allowing their recipes to be shared and only portion sizes to differ per user. This PR introduces a new data model (`llm_meal_proposals`, `llm_proposal_meals`, `meal_recipes`) and modifies the generation process to achieve this shared origin and recipe sharing, while also adding the UI and backend logic for on-demand recipe generation and display.

### GUI Integration and Testing

* Added `cmake/clamwin_gui.cmake` to build the new native Win32 C++ GUI (`clamwin`) and its test executable (`clamwin_gui_test.exe`), including test targets for real tool smoke tests and stricter update probes.
* Introduced a build version increment script (`cmake/increment_clamwin_build_version.cmake`) to generate version headers and RC files for the GUI, ensuring consistent build numbering.
* Updated `CMakeLists.txt` to include the GUI build logic and dependencies, and set up source file properties for helper modules.
* Added detailed GUI test workflow instructions and build/test commands to `README.md` and a new `build-clamav-win32.md` file, covering configuration, smoke tests, and opt-in negative/stricter probes. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5R106-R145) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-1cd50e5f70c4b0a21c2115b89d4f172b6ba64188bbefdb686decc6f605fa71d2R1-R170)

### Versioning and Licensing

* Bumped project version to 1.5.2 in `CMakeLists.txt` and `README.md`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-1e7de1ae2d059d21e1dd75d5812d5a34b0222cef273b7c3a2af62eb747f9d20aL2-R2) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L1-R1)
* Added the MIT license for the third-party `doctest` library used in GUI tests.

### Build Configuration and Compatibility

* Improved Windows version targeting in `cmake/curl.cmake` by forcing the minimum version string for older Windows builds.
* Enhanced Rust static library filtering in `cmake/legacy.cmake` with flexible Python interpreter detection, improving cross-platform compatibility.
* Made zlib-ng usage on x86 builds configurable via a CMake option in `cmake/zlib.cmake`.
* Allowed explicit cert path configuration for FreshClam in `README.md`, supporting portable/non-default layouts. This change introduces a robust system for automatically generating application screenshots for documentation. 

Key changes include:
1. **Demo Mode**: A non-intrusive demo mode in the Flutter application that can be activated by appending `?demo=true` to the URL. This mode generates synthetic waveform data, enabling reliable screenshot capture without requiring microphone access or user interaction.

3. **Documentation**: Updated `README.md` with a new section explaining how to run the screenshot generation process.
4. **Theme Fix**: Corrected a `ThemeData` assertion error where the brightness property was inconsistently set between `ThemeData` and `ColorScheme`.

The resulting screenshots are stored in `resources/screenshots/` and can be easily updated whenever the UI evolves by simply running the script.

author: bakerxiao
body:
## Summary

Cleans up duplicated progress-extraction logic across `cmd/app.go` and `cmd/jobs.go` by introducing a shared `latestProgress` helper in `cmd/helpers.go`. Also consolidates config-loading into an existing `loadConfig` helper, delegates error formatting to `output.EmitError`, and fixes a side-effect mutation bug in `runner/jobs.go` where `autoDetectCompletion` was modifying the caller's `JobMeta.Status` in memory.

**Risk Assessment:** 🟢 Low — Clean deduplication refactor with a targeted side-effect mutation fix, all tests passing with race detector.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    latestProgress["latestProgress() (added)"]
    writeError["writeError() (updated)"]
    RunApp["RunApp() (updated)"]
    backgroundJob["backgroundJob() (updated)"]
    getJob["getJob() (updated)"]
    autoDetectCompletion["autoDetectCompletion() (updated)"]
    loadConfig["loadConfig() (unchanged)"]
    EmitError["output.EmitError() (unchanged)"]
    ParseJSONL["runner.ParseJSONL() (unchanged)"]

    RunApp -- "delegates config loading" --> loadConfig
    RunApp -- "calls on timeout" --> backgroundJob
    backgroundJob -- "extracts progress via" --> latestProgress
    backgroundJob -- "parses JSONL via" --> ParseJSONL
    getJob -- "extracts progress via" --> latestProgress
    getJob -- "detects completion via" --> autoDetectCompletion
    writeError -- "delegates to" --> EmitError
```

## Key changes

- **`cmd/helpers.go`** — Added `latestProgress()` to extract the most recent progress value from parsed JSONL, replacing identical inline blocks in two call sites. Replaced hand-rolled error map construction in `writeError()` with a call to `output.EmitError`.
- **`cmd/app.go`** — Replaced inline config-loading boilerplate (cwd + `config.Load`) with a call to the existing `loadConfig()` helper. Swapped inline progress extraction for `latestProgress()`.
- **`cmd/jobs.go`** — Swapped inline progress extraction for `latestProgress()`.
- **`runner/jobs.go`** — Fixed `autoDetectCompletion` to write a copy of `JobMeta` to disk instead of mutating the caller's pointer, preventing unintended side-effect where an in-memory status could be prematurely set to `"completed"`.

## How was this tested

All tests pass with race detector enabled (`make test-race`).

author: rsubtil
body:
Different approach from #114457 (cc @kbieganski)

Closes #111175 (cannot reproduce myself, but has received feedback from @tmilker & @rsa17826
 it works)

Instead of the original solution of always propagating the `stopped` signal even when no debugger session was active (breaks DAP since it expects the signal to be emitted once and when a session is active), this approach does so only if the debug server is valid or the debugger session is active. If neither of those happen, then we still stop the debugging session but "internally", without propagating the `stopped` signal.

(cc @m4gr3d due to f713a20c94478bef3a8bc0e9300c24d37987b984 / #108518, just to double check this doesn't reintroduce an issue you fixed)

author: jose37456
body:
## Description
`_search_google` and `_search_brave` used synchronous `httpx.get()` and `time.sleep()` inside `@mcp.tool()` handlers. In the asyncio-based Hive framework, this blocks the entire event loop during network I/O and rate-limit backoffs, stalling all other concurrent agents/nodes.

This PR converts both helpers to `async def`, switches to `httpx.AsyncClient` with `await`, and replaces `time.sleep()` with `await asyncio.sleep()` — matching the pattern already used by `web_scrape_tool.py`.

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix

## Related Issues
Fixes #5332

## Changes Made
- `tools/src/aden_tools/tools/web_search_tool/web_search_tool.py` — added `import asyncio`; made `_search_google`, `_search_brave`, and `web_search` all `async def`; replaced `httpx.get()` with `httpx.AsyncClient` + `await client.get()`; replaced `time.sleep()` with `await asyncio.sleep()`; removed now-unused `import time`

author: qtpi-bonding
body:
Problem

  On iOS (and macOS), PowerSyncSQLCipherOpenFactory fails with:

  SqliteException(21): Could not load extension

  This happens in PowerSyncOpenFactory.enableExtension() when it calls
  sqlite3.ensureExtensionLoaded(), which internally calls sqlite3_auto_extension() and
  gets SQLITE_MISUSE (21) back.

  Root cause: The sqlite3 Dart package's _defaultOpen() on iOS tries
  sqlite3.framework/sqlite3 and CSQLite.framework/CSQLite first (for
  sqlite3_flutter_libs). Neither exists when using sqlcipher_flutter_libs, so it falls
  back to DynamicLibrary.process() (RTLD_DEFAULT). RTLD_DEFAULT resolves to Apple's
  system sqlite3 before SQLCipher, and Apple's system sqlite3 has extension loading
  disabled — so sqlite3_auto_extension returns SQLITE_MISUSE.

  Fix

  The Android override already handles this correctly by explicitly loading
  libsqlcipher.so via openCipherOnAndroid(). This PR adds the equivalent for iOS and
  macOS: explicitly load SQLCipher.framework/SQLCipher by path, bypassing RTLD_DEFAULT
  entirely.

  Testing

  Verified on a physical iOS device (iPhone). Before this fix the app crashed
  immediately on launch. After this fix SQLCipher initialises correctly and PRAGMA
  cipher_version returns a result.

author: marsteel
body:
📝 Summary
This PR introduces significant performance upgrades and user experience improvements. Key highlights include a Smart Preloading System, Persistent Metadata Caching, and Automated Onboarding, along with critical fixes for a more seamless viewing experience.

✨ Key Changes
1. Smart Preloading & Rate Limiting (Performance)
Playback-Relative Prioritization: Rewrote the VTT download logic to prioritize segments starting from the current playback time. This ensures subtitles are available immediately when jumping or skipping through a video.
Seek-Based Re-prioritization: Added a listener for seeked events. If a user skips to a non-buffered timestamp, the extension instantly re-prioritizes the download queue to fetch nearby segments first.
Safe Fetching (Rate Limiting): Implemented a 50ms delay between segment requests to emulate human-like traffic and prevent server-side throttling or temporary blocking by CDNs.
2. Metadata Caching (Reliability)
Persistent Video Mapping: Subtitle language-to-URL mappings are now cached in chrome.storage.local for the 10 most recently viewed videos.
Instant Recovery: Allows the popup to populate the language list immediately upon opening, surviving page reloads or tab switching without waiting for a new master playlist interception.
3. Smart User Onboarding (UX)
Auto-Notification: Implemented logic to automatically open the localized Changelog page upon installation or version update to keep users informed.
Smart Localization: Automatically detects the browser's UI language during the first installation and sets it as the default secondaryLang.
4. Critical Bug Fixes (Stability)
Subtitle Persistence Fix: Resolved a bug where subtitles would remain on screen after navigating away from the video player to the main menu.
Style Overrides: Standardized the use of setProperty(..., 'important') for all custom styles to ensure user preferences correctly override Disney+'s native CSS.
5. Documentation & Maintenance
Localized Documentation: Launched a professional, multi-language documentation site (index + privacy policy) mirroring the aesthetic of reference industry tools.
Repository Cleanup: Added .gitignore and removed system-specific files (.DS_Store) to maintain a clean codebase.

🧪 Verification
 Jump to the middle of a long movie (2h+) and verify that subtitles appear within ~1s.
 Verify in the Network tab that VTT segments are fetched with a visible 50ms gap.
 Refresh a video page and confirm the popup still shows the correct language list instantly.
 Navigate back to the home screen from a playing video and confirm the subtitle overlay disappears.

author: copilot
body:
This PR adds five modular market-structure detectors using only existing MT5-available data (price, spread proxy, tick volume), and integrates them into the current scoring/memory pipeline without removing safeguards, governance, risk guards, or execution controls.  
Each detector now emits explicit confidence metadata and contributes to automatic weak-pattern pruning through existing intelligence scoring.

- **Detector modules added (feature-layer, no architecture rewrite)**
  - `liquidity_sweep`: detects recent high/low sweeps, stop-run characteristics, and liquidity zones.
  - `compression_expansion`: measures contraction and computes expansion/breakout probability.
  - `session_behavior`: tracks Asia/London/New York behavior with session-conditioned win-rate/volatility context.
  - `market_regime`: classifies `trend | range | high_volatility` and applies regime-aware confidence impact.
  - `execution_quality`: tracks slippage proxy, spread conditions, and fill-timing proxy from bar cadence.

- **Pipeline integration**
  - Registered all detectors in `OversoulDirector.module_map`.
  - Added detector execution in `run_advanced_modules(...)` and included outputs in `module_results/module_health`.
  - Reused existing aggregation path (`confidence_delta` + direction voting), so detector outputs feed signal scoring immediately.

- **Confidence + pruning contract**
  - Standardized detector outputs include:
    - `confidence`
    - `confidence_level` (`low|medium|high`)
    - `confidence_delta`
    - `reasons` / `metrics`
  - Weak setups are explicitly marked (e.g. `weak_pattern_pruned`) and naturally down-ranked by existing strategy intelligence pruning.

- **Memory persistence + scoring contribution**
  - Detector payloads are persisted via existing snapshot memory flow (`pattern_memory -> advanced_state.module_results`).
  - Detector names are included in `feature_contributors`, making contribution traceable in live learning artifacts.

```python
# Example detector payload now emitted by new modules
{
    "module": "liquidity_sweep",
    "state": "computed",
    "direction_vote": "sell",
    "confidence": 0.74,
    "confidence_level": "medium",
    "confidence_delta": 0.06,
    "reasons": ["buy_side_liquidity_swept", "stop_run_pattern"],
    "metrics": {
        "volume_ratio": 1.42,
        "liquidity_zones": [{"kind": "recent_high", "price": 2034.2}]
    }
}
```

author: sanjusoftware
body:
This change refactors the authentication and tenant resolution logic to eliminate the need for a custom 'bank_id' claim in the Identity Provider (IDP). 

Key changes:
1. **Tenant Resolution**: `AuthorityMappingService` now resolves the `bank_id` by looking up the `BankConfiguration` in the database using the combination of the token's `issuer` (`iss`) and `client_id` (extracted from `azp` or `aud` claims). 
2. **Security Enhancement**: Any `bank_id` claim present in the token is now explicitly ignored, preventing potential spoofing by IDP administrators.
3. **Database Constraints**: The `BankConfiguration` entity was updated to enforce uniqueness on the `(issuer_url, client_id)` pair, allowing different banks to share an IDP tenant while maintaining isolation.
4. **Data Consistency**: `BankConfigurationService` now normalizes `issuer_url` (removing trailing slashes) upon creation or update to ensure reliable matching.
5. **Testing**: Introduced `AuthorityMappingServiceTest` and updated `JwtAuthConverterTest` to cover various claim extraction scenarios (String aud, List aud, azp precedence) and error cases (inactive bank, missing configuration).

This pull request introduces two major improvements to the codebase: (1) a modular refactor of form widgets for better maintainability, and (2) the complete removal of Zod-based validation and schema generation from the form core, making validation fully external and the form purely presentational. Additionally, documentation and code comments have been updated to reflect these architectural changes, and a brainstorming session document has been added to guide future development.

**Form System Refactor and Validation Architecture:**

- **Modular Widget Architecture:**  
  Each form widget is now implemented in its own file under `widgets/`, with a unified props interface and no usage of `any` types. The main dispatcher (`ts-form-field.tsx`) now only routes to these widgets, improving code clarity and maintainability. All widget exports are consistently named, and accessibility improvements (e.g., unique IDs, `readonly` support) have been made. Comprehensive tests ensure correctness. (_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/1-1-modularni-architektura-widgetu.md_)

- **Removal of Zod Validation and Schema Generation:**  
  All internal references to Zod, including the schema generator and resolver, have been removed from the form core (`index.tsx`, `ts-form-schema.ts` deleted). The form now relies solely on external validation, with errors passed via props. This makes the form easier to integrate and decouples it from any specific validation library. Types and tests have been updated accordingly, and documentation now reflects this external validation approach.

**Documentation Updates:**

- **Docs and Readme Alignment:**  
  All documentation (`README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`) now describes the form system as using "React Hook Form + External validation" instead of Zod. References to the internal schema generator have been removed, and instructions clarify that validation must be handled externally by the parent component. **Planning and Future Direction:**

- **Brainstorming Session Artifact:**  
  Added a detailed record of a brainstorming session outlining the architectural vision for a metadata-driven, highly automated documentation and playground platform. This document details steps for further generalization, automation, and integration towards a low-code ERP platform.

These changes collectively modernize the form system, making it more modular, maintainable, and flexible for integration in a variety of projects.

author: cthumuluru-crdb
body:
Previously, serverController.start() synchronously called startInitialSecondaryTenantServers(), which blocked on startAndWaitForRunningServer() for each tenant. If any secondary tenant failed to start (e.g., failed upgrade, corrupted state), the entire node's PreStart() would never return, preventing the system tenant SQL service from accepting connections.

This change removes the synchronous startup path. Secondary tenant servers are now started exclusively by the existing async "mark-tenant-services" loop, which already handles errors with logging and retry, and respects context cancellation. This loop fires ~1 second after PreStart() completes, so tenants still start promptly without risking node availability.

This change doesn't impact external tenants since server controller is only responsible to start shared tenants.

---

### Health endpoints behavior after this change

- Health endpoint for system tenant can be reached at http://localhost:8080/health?ready=1&nofallback=true
- In case of shared tenants HTTP requests are multiplexed over same listener. Health endpoints for a specific secondary tenant can be reached at http://localhost:8080/health?ready=1&cluster=t3&nofallback=true. 

As soon as system tenant is started, health endpoint for system tenant starts reporting healthy and is ready to accept SQL connections. Since secondary tenants are started asynchronously, there will be a _short_ period of time where the health checks for secondary tenants would return 503. SQL connection attempts with in this window will fail.

Prior to this change, since secondary tenants are started synchronously, health endpoint for system tenant starts reporting healthy only after all tenants are ready. With this change, each tenant reports its health depending on when it is ready to accept connections.

NB: `nofallback=false` health check request for a secondary tenant silently falls back and returns system tenant's health.

---

Fixes: #96547

Release note (bug fix): Fixed a bug where a CockroachDB node could hang during startup if a secondary tenant (shared-process) server failed to initialize, blocking the system tenant from accepting connections.

author: megheaiulian
body:
Fixes #5

- Accept `.#flow`, `./path#flow`, or `.#nixosConfigurations.flow` as input
- Derive full attribute for nix-drv: `.#nixosConfigurations.flow.config.system.build.toplevel`
- Derive short attribute for nixos-rebuild --flake: `.#flow`

This allows users to pass either format and both modules work correctly.

The `nix-drv` module needs the full path including `nixosConfigurations`, while `nixos-rebuild --flake` needs just the hostname since it prepends `nixosConfigurations` internally.

author: tomtom215
body:
## Summary
This PR implements Phase 7 features including task state transitions (Submitted → Pending), support for `return_immediately` mode, context-based task continuation with validation, push notification delivery during streaming, and protocol improvements (A2A version headers, content-type standardization, query parameter parsing).

## Key Changes

### Task State & Lifecycle
- Renamed `TaskState::Submitted` to `TaskState::Pending` to better represent the initial task state
- Updated task creation to use `Pending` state instead of `Submitted`
- Added support for `return_immediately` configuration flag that returns a task immediately without waiting for completion

### Context-Based Task Continuation
- Implemented `find_task_by_context()` to locate existing tasks by context_id
- Added validation to reject mismatched task_id when a context_id is provided (context/task mismatch rejection)
- Tasks with the same context_id create new task instances with stored_task references

### Push Notifications
- Integrated push notification delivery into the event collection loop
- Added `deliver_push()` method to send notifications for StatusUpdate and ArtifactUpdate events
- Push notifications are delivered for each streaming event when push configs exist

### REST Dispatcher Improvements
- Implemented tenant prefix routing (`/tenants/{tenant}/` paths)
- Added query parameter parsing for GET requests (historyLength, contextId, status, pageSize, etc.)
- Extended subscribe endpoint to accept both POST and GET methods
- Refactored dispatch logic to separate tenant extraction and route handling

### Protocol & Headers
- Added A2A protocol constants: `A2A_VERSION` (1.0.0), `A2A_CONTENT_TYPE` (application/a2a+json), `A2A_VERSION_HEADER`
- Updated all HTTP responses to include A2A-Version and standardized content-type headers
- Applied to both REST and JSON-RPC dispatchers

### Client Transport
- Updated REST transport to append query parameters for GET/DELETE requests
- Added query string builder for converting JSON params to URL query format
- Updated both REST and JSON-RPC transports to send A2A version headers
- Added body truncation utility for error messages (max 512 chars)

### Agent Card
- Restored `state_transition_history` field to `AgentCapabilities` (was previously removed)
- Updated example agent to include the field in capability declarations

### Testing
- Added Phase 7 handler tests: return_immediately, task continuation, context mismatch rejection, interceptor rejection
- Added dispatch tests for A2A version headers, tenant prefix routing, GET subscribe support
- Updated error status mapping: PushNotSupported now returns 400 instead of 501

## Implementation Details
- Query parameter parsing uses simple string splitting (no URL decoding for now)
- Push notification delivery is async and non-blocking
- Task continuation validates that explicit task_id matches the context-found task
- Tenant extraction strips `/tenants/{tenant}/` prefix and passes tenant to handlers

author: sgrebnov
body:
## Which issue does this PR close?

Fixes a panic (`Column index out of bounds for projected expressions`) when a query applies a scalar function to a metadata column (e.g. `SELECT upper(_location) FROM t`).

The existing guard in `try_swapping_with_projection` only checked top-level `Column` expressions via `downcast_ref::<Column>()`. When a metadata column was nested inside a function call (e.g. `upper(_location)`), the downcast returned `None`, the metadata reference was missed, and the projection was incorrectly pushed down into the file source — causing an out-of-bounds panic.

**Fix:** Use `collect_columns()` to find all `Column` references within each projection expression, including those nested inside function calls, and check them against `projected_metadata_positions`.

- added backend financial-context helpers to retain recent income/expense/partial context

- kept income and partial signals additive without forcing false expense certainty

## Summary

- Adds `IPromptService` / `PromptService` with 7 prompt-builder methods: lesson plan, vocabulary, grammar, exercises, conversation, reading, homework
- `GenerationContext` record captures all lesson + student context (language, CEFR level, topic, style, student profile, existing notes, lesson summary)

Haiku wraps JSON in markdown code fences despite the "no code fences" instruction in the system prompt; Sonnet complies cleanly. `StripCodeFences` helper added to integration tests as a preview — T13's response parser will need the same logic before deserializing Claude output.

body:
## Summary

Add conflict resolution module for LicenseDB data synchronization as part of GSoC 2026 project. This module handles conflicts that may arise when synchronizing license and obligation data from LicenseDB.

## Changes

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `ResolutionStrategy.java` | Enum: REPLACE, SKIP, MERGE, MANUAL |
| `ConflictResult.java` | Result container for resolution decisions |
| `ConflictConfig.java` | Configuration properties for default strategies |
| `ConflictResolver.java` | Interface for conflict resolution |
| `LicenseConflictResolver.java` | License-specific conflict resolution |
| `ObligationConflictResolver.java` | Obligation-specific conflict resolution |

## Resolution Strategies

| Strategy | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `REPLACE` | Overwrite local data with LicenseDB data |
| `SKIP` | Keep local data, ignore LicenseDB updates |
| `MERGE` | Combine data (prefer non-null values) |
| `MANUAL` | Flag for manual administrator review |

## Configuration

```yaml
licensedb:
  conflict-resolution:
    default-license-strategy: REPLACE
    default-obligation-strategy: REPLACE
    audit-enabled: true
    audit-log-path: logs/license-db-conflicts.log
```

## Usage

```java
@Autowired
private LicenseConflictResolver licenseConflictResolver;

public void syncLicense(License incoming) {
    License existing = licenseService.getLicenseByShortname(incoming.getShortname());
    ConflictResult<License> result = licenseConflictResolver.resolve(
        incoming, 
        existing, 
        ResolutionStrategy.REPLACE
    );
    
    if (result.isRequiresManualReview()) {
        // Queue for manual review
    }
}
```

- [x] Files compile without errors
- [x] Follows SW360 code style
- [x] EPL-2.0 license headers included
- [x] No new dependencies

## Dependencies

- Depends on: PR #3686 (LicenseDB configuration)
- Related: PR #3898 (Data transformation layer)

## Related

Fixes #3899

author: murrellb
body:
## Summary

  This fixes a set of Julia 1.12 regressions in Zygote's compiler integration.

  The main breakages were:
  - regressions around Julia 1.12 global access lowering
  - failures in generated pullback code for keyword/default-wrapper methods
  - forward-mode failures on new 1.12 internal IR intrinsics

  These regressions showed up in small MWEs and in downstream code paths such as ChainStorm on Julia 1.12, including GPU-backed training-style workloads.

  ## What Was Broken

  ### 1. Global access on Julia 1.12

  Julia 1.12 changed the lowered/internal representation of module global access. Zygote was still assuming the older form, which caused incorrect differentiation results for code that reads globals or module bindings.

  ### 2. Keyword/default-wrapper pullback generation

  On Julia 1.12, some synthesized keyword/default-wrapper methods could lead Zygote to emit malformed lowered `:isdefined` expressions in generated pullback `CodeInfo`.

  That invalid IR could then fail during code generation, including the crash path hit by a reduced ChainStorm reproducer.

  ### 3. Forward-mode interaction with new 1.12 internals

  Julia 1.12 introduced internal IR operations that should be treated as non-differentiable metadata from Zygote's perspective. Without that handling, forward-mode paths could fail or hard-error.

  ## Fixes

  ### Reverse mode / globals

  - instrument `Core.getglobal` in reverse-mode compilation
  - add an adjoint for `getglobal`

  This restores correct behavior for gradients that depend on module/global access.

  ### Pullback generation / kw wrappers

  - sanitize invalid lowered `Expr(:isdefined, ...)` nodes in generated pullback `CodeInfo` before returning it

  This fixes the Julia 1.12 kw/default-wrapper crash path without changing user-facing semantics.

  ### Forward mode / 1.12 internals

  - treat new Julia 1.12 metadata-style internal operations as non-differentiable
  - guard those additions so Julia 1.11 remains compatible
  - stop hard-failing on 1.12 `foreigncall` IR in the forward compiler path

  ## Tests

  Adds/updates tests for:
  - Julia 1.12 global access regressions
  - Julia 1.12 forward-mode regressions
  - a minimal keyword-wrapper/logging reproducer for the pullback-generation failure
  - Flux-facing MWEs (`Flux.normalise` / `Flux.LayerNorm`) that exercise the same fixed paths

  ## Validation

  Verified on Julia 1.12:
  - targeted `compiler`, `forward`, and `flux` test items pass
  - reduced ChainStorm GPU backward paths now run on GPU 0
  - a fixed-batch ChainStorm benchmark runs successfully on both Julia 1.11 and 1.12

  The remaining known Julia 1.12 issue is an inference regression for `usesmod`: the gradient value is correct, but inference is wider than on Julia 1.11.

## What changed ## How to test ## Checklist - [ ] I ran relevant checks locally (`make fmt`, `make lint`, `make test`) - [ ] I updated docs, comments, or examples when needed - [ ] This PR is scoped and ready for review

Greptile Summary

This PR introduces the first functional backend for the translation async pipeline: a Postgres-backed job store (Bun + pgx), an outbox-event pattern for durable async dispatch, a stub queue publisher, a GCP Cloud Functions handler for processing queued jobs, and wires all of these into the existing gRPC service handlers. Key changes: - `internal/translation/{app,store,queue,worker,config}` — new packages providing the job lifecycle, Bun models, broker-agnostic publisher interface, stub adapter, worker processor, and environment config - `api/services/translation/service.go` — all four gRPC RPCs now delegate to `app.Service`; `mapError` correctly translates application errors to gRPC status codes - `apps/translation-service/main.go` — bootstraps Postgres, stub publisher, and app service from config - `apps/translation-worker-gcp/function.go` — CloudEvent-driven GCF handler with lazy-initialised processor (correct `package function`, mutex-guarded singleton, retries on transient init errors) - `docs/adr/2026-03-15-translation-async-stub-design.md` — clearly documents decisions and deferred work Notable issues found: - **Orphan job on publish failure** (`internal/translation/app/service.go`): the job and outbox event are committed in a transaction *before* `publisher.Publish()` is called. When the stub is replaced with a real adapter, any publish error will leave an untrackable orphan job in the database while the gRPC caller receives a failure response. The deferred outbox-dispatcher TODO is the right fix, but the current code needs to handle the error path so it doesn't silently corrupt state. - **Redundant double-encoding** (`internal/translation/app/service.go`): `encodeJSON(queuedPayload)` is called twice because `EventID` is set after the first encode. Setting `EventID` before the first encode eliminates the wasted marshal. - **Clock bypass in `UpdateJobStatus`** (`internal/translation/store/repository.go`): `updated_at` is stamped with a raw `time.Now().UTC()` call instead of accepting the caller's injected clock, causing a subtle inconsistency with the `completed_at` value on terminal transitions and making the repository harder to test deterministically.

Confidence Score: 3/5

- Safe to merge as a stub, but the publish-failure correctness gap must be addressed before wiring in a real Pub/Sub adapter. - The implementation is well-structured and the stub publisher never fails in practice, so there are no current runtime regressions. However, the orphan-job bug in `CreateJob` is a real correctness issue that will be triggered the moment the stub is replaced with a live adapter — and the PR explicitly TODOs that replacement. The double-encoding and clock-bypass issues are lower severity but add technical debt. No migrations are included yet (acknowledged as deferred), so the service will fail at startup against a real DB, limiting blast radius during this stub phase. - Pay close attention to `internal/translation/app/service.go` (publish-after-commit ordering) and `internal/translation/store/repository.go` (clock handling in `UpdateJobStatus`).

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | internal/translation/app/service.go | Core application service wiring jobs, outbox events, and queue publishing. Contains a correctness issue: the transaction commits before `Publish` is called, so a publish failure leaves an orphan job in the DB that the gRPC caller never learns about. Also encodes the outbox payload twice redundantly. | | internal/translation/worker/worker.go | Processor handles individual job events for the GCF path. `MarkOutboxEventProcessed` runs outside the job-state transaction (addressed in a previous review thread). `buildStubOutcome` correctly generates placeholder translations for both string and file job types. | | apps/translation-worker-gcp/function.go | GCF CloudEvent handler with lazy-initialised processor via mutex guard. Package declaration is correctly `function` (not `main`). Initialization correctly retries on error (no `sync.Once` poisoning). `decodePayload` correctly unpacks the Pub/Sub CloudEvent envelope and validates required fields. | | internal/translation/store/repository.go | Bun-backed repository for jobs and outbox events. `UpdateJobStatus` uses `time.Now().UTC()` directly for `updated_at` rather than accepting the caller's clock value, creating a small inconsistency with `completed_at` on terminal transitions. | | apps/translation-service/main.go | Service entrypoint now wires Postgres, stub publisher, and app service together from config. Clean extraction of `defaultListenAddr` into `ServiceConfig.ListenAddr`. | | internal/translation/queue/stub.go | Log-backed stub publisher that never returns an error. Intentionally minimal as a placeholder for the real Pub/Sub adapter. | | internal/translation/store/postgres.go | Opens a pgx-backed Bun DB with immediate ping validation. `Close` correctly handles a nil DB. Straightforward and correct. | | internal/translation/config/config.go | Environment-based config for both service and worker. Defaults `TRANSLATION_QUEUE_DRIVER` to `gcp-pubsub` and `LISTEN_ADDR` to `:8080`. Clean and straightforward. | | api/services/translation/service.go | gRPC service handler now correctly wires through to the app service for all four RPCs. `mapError` properly maps `ErrInvalidArgument` and `ErrNotFound` to gRPC status codes. |

Paste (Ctrl+V) and drag-drop bypassed the model entirely — content was written directly into the contentEditable DOM without updating `model`. When the user saved, `getHtml()` returned the stale pre-paste model, the server stored the old/empty content, and `load()` reloaded it — making the pasted content vanish.
